correctness.rationale: Full concept-extent definitions and join/meet quasi-identities are reconstructed. A complete Prüfer-labelled-tree enumeration for all 18,249 trees of size at most seven proves P7 is the unique offending class (2,520/16,807 at order seven). A direct closed-extent witness proves the path fails. Complement-graph connected components induce direct-product concept lattices. Rare seven-path count has exact mean ((n)_4(m)_3+(n)_3(m)_4)q^6/2, converging to ((alpha^3+alpha^4)/2)t^6; the dependency-graph overlap and non-isolation bounds give total variation O(n^-1/6) for q=t n^-7/6. Larger components and cycles contribute O(n^-1/6), while second moments prove supercritical failure when nq -> 0. The embedded verifier runs successfully; finite computations are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete first-transition classification of a central lattice identity gives a distinct natural invariant from distributivity: six-vertex path contexts can be semidistributive despite nondistributivity, while P7 is the first minimal semidistributivity obstruction. The sharp scale n^-7/6 and explicit α-dependent Poisson law quantify a previously missing phase in the standard random formal-context regime. This is a structural limit law, not an arbitrary small numerical gain.
